title: Pilot study of a digitally supported fall risk assessment with an app-based intervention for older adults in primary care
summary:
Many people over 70 fall at least once a year, which can lead to serious health problems. Because more people are getting older, falls are expected to become more common.
This project tests a digital tool called PIAmove*Seniors that helps general practitioners identify fall risks early and support older patients with a smartphone app. The study will take place in primary care practices in Germany and will check whether the tool is easy to use and helpful. The longt-term goal is to prevent falls in older adults.

interventions.name: The study will be conducted in primary care practices in the federal state of North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. This mixed-methods pilot study follows a single-arm design in which only the intervention is implemented, without a control group. This design enables an in-depth evaluation of data collect

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
On patient level 
•	Age ≥70 years.
•	Smartphone use at least three times per week (Android 6 or higher or IOS 14 or higher).
•	Sufficient language and cognitive skills to comprehend the study documents.

On practice level 
•	Single and group practices.
•	Licensed for statutory health insurance.
•	Computers (Windows 7 or higher) with internet access.
Exclusion criteria:
On patient level 
•	Acute illnesses or injuries that impair balance, mobility, or the ability to engage in unsupervised home-based physical training (e.g., fractures, amputations).
•	Neurological disorders associated with pronounced motor limitations, including advanced Parkinson’s disease, advanced-stage multiple sclerosis, severe hemiplegia after stroke, and unexplained syncope.
•	Severe dementia. 
•	Severe visual or auditory impairments (e.g., blindness, deafness).
•	Accommodation in a retirement home.

On practice level 
•	Exclusively private medical services.
•	No digital practice management system.
